definitions.volume_index: weekly hard RESISTANCE sets (or sets per exercise when the slot count is constant) / week 1 x 100. Athletic work (plyo contacts, throws, sprints, Olympic lifts) is tracked separately.
definitions.total_index: athlete skeletons only: all working sets incl. athletic (excluding med-ball throws and conditioning) / week 1 x 100
definitions.set_counting: v1: 1 hard set = 1.0 to the main mover + 0.25 to each helper (COACH-ANSWER VOL-09); dips 0.5 triceps + 0.5 chest (LIB-16); a 10/10 unilateral set = 1 set (UNI-01). Athletic sets (plyo, ballistic, throws, Olympic, sprints) never count toward muscles (VOL-10). Pelland 0.5 is kept only as a research comparison (12_volume_algorithm_v1).
definitions.ref_sets: v1 mode grids: weekly hard sets of one reference big muscle at the level start (L1 10, L2 15, L3 20), moved with the volume engine bank rules and capped at the level cap (L1 14, L2 22, L3 25)

verification_log: CrossFit macro (2.2, OBS_CF_MACRO): the claim that 'each block restarts aerobic and WOD levels higher' was WRONG. Aerobic runs 1-2-3 | 1-2-3-4 | 2-3-4 and WODs 2-3 | 2-3-4 | 2-3-4, so only block 3 restarts aerobic higher. 'Resistance rides with strength' is false for block 1 (FEB-MARCH resistance alone, APRIL strength + power). Added: the AUGUST grid marks 2 WOD days at WOD level 3.

CrossFit FULL TIME '+5.5 %/week' (rule 4, table 2.3) was presented as an observed rate. The macro never walks strength L1-L2-L3-L4 in consecutive months (L1 APRIL, L3 JUNE, L4 JULY, L2 OCT/NOV), so the rate is relabelled INFERRED (a hypothetical walk of the dose table).

Effort grammar (rule 6/R6, 5.1, strength rules) was presented as OBSERVED 'nuance = unilateral MAX, survival = isolation ALL'. It is a splice of STRENGTH-12 slot names with STRENGTH-8 effort words. In STRENGTH-8 and the CONJUGATE draft the 'MAX' rows are pull-ups / DB rows, alt incline DB bench and lunges, and the 'ALL' rows are RFE lunges / staggered DL and bicep curls. The class mapping is now marked INFERRED.

Dynamic-effort effort: STRENGTH-8 and the CONJUGATE draft label the fast rows '1RIR' (4T D18/D21). The STRENGTH_8 skeleton had borrowed STRENGTH-12's 'FAST RPE6 or about 60-70%' as if it were STRENGTH-8's own label. Fixed, flagged as a conflict, and added as an open question.

STRENGTH_8 week-1 doses were wrong. DE sets are 5 on Thursday but 3 on Saturday (B18/B21). Accessory sets are 3-4, not 3. The 'ALL' rows are 2-3 x '8/8' (not '8/8' or 10). The 10-rep rows are the 'MAX' rows. Added: the green ladder fill also covers B17 (plyo) and B21. The week-8 weekly set count of 10 is now marked INFERRED, and the 'the work' label for the plyo row is attributed to the CONJUGATE draft (M21).

STRENGTH_12 week 1: 'TATE PRESS' 3x20 was attributed to 'the survival'. It sits in the Wednesday NUANCE slot (N15). Also: main-lift reps per session are 18-20 in weeks 1-10 but 14 in weeks 11-12, not 'held 18-20'. The STRENGTH-12 'A/B weeks' are an analyst label: there are no 'A WEEK'/'B WEEK' cells.

HYPERTROPHY_12/6 effort: AESTHETICS-12 writes no RIR/RPE. Its rows were marked OBSERVED with '1-2 RIR' / '1 RIR' / '0-1 RIR' efforts borrowed from AESTHETICS-8 col D, so effort is now marked INFERRED. Also flagged: in weeks 4-6 the SETS row says 4 while the rep string lists 3 numbers before '-20'. Reading '-20' as the isolation reps is INFERRED.
AESTHETICS-12 week-12 overreach: chest (32.5 sets) was omitted from the '33-35 sets' list.

HYBRID-8: the evidence range was 'rows 76-101'; the program starts at row 74. Added: the header SETS/REPS do not match the written bench (3x6, 3x6, 3x8, 3x8, 3x10, 3x10, 4x6, 4x8) or the Olympic sets. Also added: the unexplained row 79 (2,2,3,2,2,3,2,2); that the AMRAP row is not tied to a day (Saturday attribution INFERRED); and the full Thursday lunge ladder (wk6-8 'FF & RFE dcontra', 'RFE contra', 'RFE ipsi' were missing).
HYBRID_12 week 8 claimed 'WODs L3 (3/wk)'; the AUGUST grid shows only 2 WOD days. Noted.

Isolation rep ladder '15 -> 20 -> 30 -> 40' (rules 5/R5, L02, governor) is not a single observed ladder. The FAT BURN slots are leg ext/curl 15-20-40-40, arms 30-30-30-40 and side raises 15-15-20-20. L02's '+33-50 % per step' was wrong: the steps are +33 %, +100 %, 0 %.

UL/PPL level ladder: PPL legs are 2x8 / 3x10 / 4x8, not 2x12, so 'lower compounds 2x12' holds only for UL; this is a second anomaly. Isolations are NOT fixed at every level: PPL side raises, rear-delt flies and upright rows follow the compound ladder (3x15 -> 4x8). PPL A-drills start at 2x'8/8'. Only UL curls are 'MAX REPS'. 'About +3 %/week' corrected to +3-4 %/week (+3.7 % at 4 weeks per level).

Pain rule (section 10, governor, autoregulation) was cited as 'A6/A7' with a quote containing 'going unilateral'. That wording is only in the ATHLETIC FULL BODY tab (A6); UL/PPL A7 mention split grips only. The quote is now verbatim and attributed to the right tab.

Throws: 'always R/L pairs' was wrong. Chest pass, overhead throw, squat to chest pass, slams, back-to-wall scoops and sit-up throws are bilateral single entries. Sit-up throws are 1x20 in BALLISTICS (A70:B71) but 10 in the boxing list (F68:F69).

Olympic lifts: the coach's 'OPTIONAL PIECE' label on every BASEBALL Olympic row (CI33, DA33, DS33, BC51, BU51, CM51, DD50) was missing. Added to the ladders, the PRE_8 skeleton and the open questions.

BASEBALL blocks are labelled only 'BLOCK 1/2/3'. Their off-season / pre-season / in-season reading is now marked INFERRED (Block 3 dates fall in the calendar's 'IN SEASON' months). Date cells corrected: AH61 'March 20 - 26', AU61 'March 27th - 31st', DN60 '04/24 to 04/28'. 'Dated March 20 - April 28' is corrected to weeks 3-8 only.

Deload rule (rule 7/R7/D4): '3 sets x 8 at RPE ~7' was presented as observed. Only STRENGTH-12 writes an RPE, and its deload is 3 x 4; AESTHETICS-12 is 3 x '8/8/8-12' and BASEBALL is 3 x 8. The unified default is now marked INFERRED. D1/plan shapes now list the 8-week exceptions: BOXING ends at a peak, HYBRID-8 has no deload, the CrossFit class tests only.

12-week shape (rule 3/R3/D2/section 7): 'weeks 8-12 = new phase with intensifiers, week 12 = RPE 10 / 5 sets' merged two programs. Only AESTHETICS-12 changes the menu and adds intensifiers (5 sets + MYO); STRENGTH-12 keeps its A/B menu and peaks at 7 x 2 @ RPE 10.

Rule 9/R10 'athletic work never disappears' now lists its exceptions: the boxer's base weeks have zero plyos, the BASEBALL Block 1 'wk 8' recovery week has no plyos or throws, and deloads keep only 1-2 Part A sets.

BOXING: the 'Always go for 1-3 RIR...' quote in the base-week effort is not in the BOXING tab; it comes from UL/PPL A6 and ATHLETIC A5 and is now marked as an INFERRED default. Also clarified: working-set counts are component sets; the week colour groups are 1-2 / 3-4 / 5-7 / 8; and the week-8 detail (depth drops, SL march jumps, squirrel jumps, side+front raises stay at 2 sets). Sport table: upper-body work after week 2 is not 'removed' - it survives inside combos.
FAT BURN circuits are not 'one lower and one upper'. Mon/Fri weeks are mixed full-body + core; in Tue/Thu weeks, Tuesday is upper + core and Thursday is lower + core.

Worked governor example (4.6): the text said the focus muscle (chest +6) gets the largest increase, but biceps gains more (+7, 12 -> 19). The per-week increments are 0.21-0.84 sets, not '+0.4-0.6'. The reverse mapping would add ~0.36 sets/week to biceps, not ~0.2.
Floors (4.4): '6-8 sets for maintenance' was attributed to Schoenfeld 2017. It is not a Schoenfeld finding and is now marked INFERRED (practitioner range + Spiering 2021).
EFFORT '8 - That was perfect': the dropdown label is observed; calling it the 'bullseye'/target is an inference and is now labelled so (5.2, governor modifier, autoregulation).
Plyo ladders: the within-phase rules (bilateral before unilateral, etc.) and the BALLISTICS-phase-to-Sheet23-zone mapping are read from list order and were labelled OBSERVED. They are now INFERRED.

Science - RPE chart: the 10-rep column and RPE7 x 8 did not match the RTS/Tuchscherer chart. Corrected to RPE9x10 70.7, RPE8x10 68.0, RPE7x8 70.7, RPE7x10 65.3 (all were 1-2 points high). The chart is attributed to RTS, not Zourdos 2016. The 1-6-rep values used for inference were correct.

Science - plyometric volume: 'newer recommendations allow up to ~200 high-intensity or ~400 low-intensity contacts/session' is NOT supported by the cited PMC7873906 table, which is a study protocol of 72 -> 126 contacts/session. Removed.

Science - RP landmarks: the cited arvo.guru page gives no per-muscle numbers, and the quoted ranges did not match RP's own guides (e.g. biceps was 4-6/10-14/14-20; RP gives MEV 8-10, MAV 14-20, MRV 20-26). Replaced with RP's published chest/quads/biceps/triceps/calves values; back is marked not extracted. The governor cross-check was updated to match.

Science - Bell 2022 (Front Sports Act Living) is a qualitative interview study of 18 coaches, not a survey (deloads ~every 4-6 weeks, ~1 week). Westside dynamic effort is ~50-60 % bar weight plus band/chain tension, not '60-70 %'. Plotkin 2022 used lower-body exercises, so it does not support a small-muscle-only rule. All three have caveats.

Sheet24 half-marathon plan: added the coach's adoption line A2 ('Program we use for all Blaze Camp Athletes who are looking to run a half marathon.') and the 1-week taper. Tab names in sources now use the exported (31-character) names instead of reconstructed full names ('& PLYOS', 'LIFTING', 'EXERCISES LIBRARY', 'CONTROL PATTERNS/CORE').

corrections: Effort grammar (rule 6, R6, L04, table 5.1, strength rules): the 'MAX' on Thursday's lunges (D20) was filed under the 3rd row 'the nuance'. On Thursday the plyo row takes 'the work' position, so the DE squat is 'the accessory' ('1RIR'), pull-ups are 'the nuance' at '2RIR' (D19, M19) and the lunges are 'the survival' at 'MAX' (D20, M20); the CONJUGATE draft is identical (M21:M24). The rule 'work 1RIR -> accessory 2RIR -> nuance MAX -> survival ALL' holds on Monday and Wednesday only. The effort word follows the exercise role, not the slot name.

Chains were listed as a dynamic-effort/speed method ('bands ~50 %, chains ~70 %' in L03, table 5.1 and the strength rules), with non-verbatim quotes '~50%'/'~70%'. In ALL ABOUT SQUATS chains are a loading tool: 'BOTTOM CHAINS' '*INTENSIONALLY SLOW YOU DOWN', 'Chains are designed for magnitude influence, loading.', 'Weght can be moderate around 70%'. Bands are the speed tool: 'Bands are designed for speed/velocity', 'Weight should be lower ranges around 50% so you can move fast'. STRENGTH-8 is consistent with this ('HEAVY CHAINED DEADLIFT' on the max-effort day H9, 'FAST BANDED DL' on the speed day H18; the draft's speed-day 'FAST CHAINED DL' CJ H22 was changed to banded in the product). Quotes made verbatim, chains removed from the speed method, and an open question added.

STRENGTH-12 load (5.2): '(OBSERVED weeks 1-7; % for weeks 8-12 INFERRED)'. The % row is filled only for weeks 1-6 (O3:T3); U3 holds the text 'MID DELOAD' and V3:Z3 are blank. RPE is observed for all 12 weeks. Fixed.

BASEBALL deload (rule 7, D4, L06, PRE_8 week 8, open question 7): the 'DELOAD WEEK' was described as 'the same template'/'same exercises'. Read cell by cell, it replays the 'WEEK 7' grid (CL43:DC58), not 'WEEK 8'. It copies many exercises unchanged ('step to chest pass', 'single leg hops', 'lay down MB presses', 'camporini deadlift', 'OH rope tricep extension', 'seal DB row'), strips the intensified versions ('banded front squats' -> 'goblet squats', 'banded kb swings' -> 'kb swings', complex -> 'front squats', 'weighted Pull ups or max reps Close grip cable lat pull down' -> 'Close grip cable lat pull down', 'heavy DB step ups ' -> ' DB step ups ') and removes 'myo set' / 'myo sets'. This generator-relevant rule was missing; it was added.

Rule 11 / R12 / L08 / lever matrix said intensification methods are concentrated in the conversion/pre-season phases and are 'rare' in-season. BASEBALL writes upper-body 'Superset - same reps' / 'Superset - max reps' pairs and banded lifts in all three blocks: Block 1 week 1 (C34), in-season Block 3 (C70, AQ69 'SUPER SET 4X', DK68 'FAST BANDED DEADLFTS'). Only the '5 of each' complexes and 'myo set' / 'myo sets' are confined to Block 2. Fixed (matrix ATH_IN: 'S(supersets, bands)').

Rule 10 / R11 said the slot skeleton 'never changes inside a plan'. It changes at phase boundaries: BOXING week 3 replaces the whole menu (the Tuesday/Friday upper days dissolve into mixed sessions); AESTHETICS-12 drops the Monday/Thursday 'TRICEP EXT.' rows after weeks 7/8 and rebuilds Friday ('RFE Lunges (bulgarian)', 'Staggered stance unilateral deadlifts', one-leg extensions/curls, leg-press MYO). Reworded to 'held inside a phase'.

Rule 13 / R9 / L01 / governor modifier / open question 12 said in-season sets are 'frozen (4 per Part)'. Only Part C/D are 4 in Block 3; Part A is 1-3 sets (mostly 3) and Part B (core) 2-4 sets or 'Accumulate' time blocks. Fixed.

BASEBALL 'partC_D_sets' said '5 in Block 2 wk6-WEEK 8'. In 'wk 6' only Monday Part C is 5 (BW52); 'WEEK 7' is 5 everywhere; 'WEEK 8' is 5 except Friday Part D (DR54 = 4); Block 1 wk7 Monday Part D is 5 (DC37). Fixed; PRE_8 week 7 now notes Friday Part D 4.

CrossFit year (2.2, OBS_CF_MACRO): the day grids were not checked against the macro. The MARCH grid schedules STRENGTH ('KNEE DOM'/'PULL'/'HIP DOM'/'PUSH') and POWER ('SNATCH'/'CLEAN') days with no level, although the macro gives MARCH resistance only. The APRIL grid keeps RESISTANCE 'LB'/'UB' days. SKILL days appear in 7 grids although the macro SKILL row is empty. 'Block 1 runs resistance alone' is now limited to the macro row; an open question was added.

HYBRID-8 (OBS, skeleton note, hybrid rules, open question 28): row 78, beside 'UPPER ACCESORY' (D78), repeats the header sets 2,2,2,3,3,3,4,4. The document said the header 'can only' govern the unwritten squat/deadlift sets. Added row 78 and softened the claim.

Athlete levels (rule 8, R8, level dial, OBS_AT_LEVELS): 89 -> 72 -> 59 were presented as plain OBSERVED sets/week. They are the decode's component counts. One written line each gives about 61 -> 53-55 -> 44. Resistance sets are flat STARTING -> MID (44 -> 44) and core sets rise at ADVANCED. The quote '3 x 1 (1RIR)' is not a cell value: H15 = 3, I15 = 1, J15 = 'DEADLIFTS (1RIR)'. Fixed; the MID deadlift reps are the date-stored '6/8' (E18), not a typed '6-8'.

L15 session budget: 'Starting 10/6/7' was wrong; the STARTING workouts have 10 / 7 / 7 lines (A12:A21, A24:A30, A33:A39). MID is 10 / 14 / 8 / 16 lines including single throw lines (10 / 4 / 8 / 6 without them). Fixed.

Throws ladder (2.4, section 9.2): the progression 'rotational subset -> full list -> 2 lists/week' is not what the sheets show. STARTING already uses one 'ALL LIST' (210/week); MID uses the 10-throw rotational subset at 2 x 10 in two sessions (400); ADVANCED uses two 'ALL LIST' sessions (420); the boxer goes 1 list -> 2 lists (190 -> 380). Fixed; which list 'ALL LIST' means is marked INFERRED.

Olympic lifts (2.4, section 9.3): 'they appear only from the second half of the off-season' is BASEBALL-only. The ATHLETIC 'STARTING' block, labelled 'First 8 weeks (8wk1)', has 'SUPERSET: Low Hang Power Cleans (mid weight) ' 3 x 8 (A36). The boxer starts 'Clean Pull/ hang Power Clean' in week 3. BASEBALL Block 1 'wk 8' still has a 4 x 6 'OLY' row with no exercise. Fixed.

BOXING-based athlete rows: the week-8 effort default 'OLY 90 %' (from the generic PEAK default) was printed on an OBSERVED BOXING row, but the BOXING tab has no % anywhere. The week-7 default 'athletic 1-2 sets' contradicts I8/I9, where depth drops and SL march jumps stay at 3 sets. Both rows now carry explicit, correctly labelled effort text.

UL/PPL ladder table (8.5): the 'PPL push/pull compounds 3 x 15 -> 3-4 x 10 -> 4 x 8' row hid two exceptions. 'Dips' go 3 x 8 -> 3 x 10 -> 4 x 'MAX'. The lat pulldown goes 3 x 15 -> 4 x 10 -> 5 x 12, so reps rise again at INTERMEDIATE. The 'Single Leg Deadlift' stays at 3 sets at INTERMEDIATE. Added. GENERAL_BEGINNER_12 note: '+3.0 %/week over 11 steps' recomputed as +2.7 %/week.

FAT BURN week 3/4 'Sets/exercise' cells ('+1 set on lead + SL RDL', '+1 set on 2nd slot') were incomplete. Week 3 also adds a set to the 1st upper slot and the arm slot and removes one from leg ext/curl and the 3rd upper slot (net +2 per half-week). Week 4 adds sets to the 2nd lower slot, leg ext/curl and the 3rd upper slot (net +3). Fixed.

HYPERTROPHY_12 Vol idx is sets per exercise. The AESTHETICS-12 slot count falls in wave 2, so the written weekly-set index is 100,100,100,133,133,133,100,129,124,124,124,154, not ...133,133,133,133,167. Added to the skeleton note.

Annual calendars (8.6, JSON annual_planning): added what was missing. Row 4 has no FEBRUARY. Row 5 marks Jul-Sep 'SOFT SEASON' as well as 'OFF SEASON'. Row 10 marks the 16 'FALL BALL' weeks 'SOFT SEASON'. The week labels skip 'WK 2'. Pro months and pro weekly are now spelled out. The calendar-to-skeleton mapping and the JSON 'mapping' string were labelled OBSERVED and are now INFERRED.

Labels presented as the coach's vocabulary that he never wrote: 'KD week / HD week' for STRENGTH-8 (the alternation is real, but the words are written only in HYBRID); 'max intent with full quality' in table 5.1 (an analyst default; the sheets write intent words only on some rows, e.g. 'Really high jump squats LOAD & jump hard', 'High Knee Runs FAST'); '1-3 RIR aka RPE 7+' (the cell reads 'Always go for 1-3 RIR (REPS IN RESERVE) aka RPE 7+'). Fixed or labelled INFERRED.

Table 2.3: the BASEBALL Block 2 rates use 5 grid-to-grid steps. Block 2 has no 'wk 3' grid ('WK 1', 'wk 2', 'wk 4' …), so over 6 calendar weeks the rates are +2.1 % (resistance) and +4.2 % (all sets). Noted in the status column.

D7 (fighter week 7) said the 'key complex/power rows ramp (3 -> 4)'. Only the knee-tuck + DB rows, 'Hang Power Clean & Press' and the hinge complex ramp; the squat complex (I22) is cut to 2 and the depth drops / SL march jumps stay at 3. Fixed.
Secondary-compound row of table 5.1 was labelled 'the accessory' only; on Thursday the 4 x 6 '2RIR' pull-ups sit in 'the nuance' row (M19). Relabelled.

Hypertrophy default dose (8.1) and worked-example base (4.6): the BYOP demo writes calves at 3 sets and 'DB Push press' 5 x '6 to 8 Reps'; the worked example's flat 3 sets per slot is now marked INFERRED.

Science: the focus ceiling '26 (inside the ~20-26 MRV region of the RP model)' is true only for biceps. RP's own guides, re-fetched, give MRV quads 14-18, triceps 16-20, chest/calves 16-24, biceps 20-26 and MRV*P up to 24-32+ / 26-35. 26 is a specialisation-level ceiling, and the non-focus 20 is above RP's quad MRV. Reworded and marked INFERRED. The Israetel comparison ('his ramp is gentler, ~+0.5 set/muscle/week') confused the INFERRED governor with what he writes: his AESTHETICS-12 STEP ladder adds about +1.1 set/muscle/week, close to RP. Fixed in 12 and SCI_RP. The deload-depth comparison now notes that 41-60 % is taper evidence, not a deload prescription. RP landmark values, the RTS chart, Issurin residuals, Bosquet taper, Gabbett ACWR, NSCA contacts and Westside DE loading were re-checked and are correct.

headline_rules: R1 Five plan modes, chosen at intake: 12-week cycle (his preferred), 8-week, 4-6-week maintenance/transition, open-ended week-by-week, and yearly. No 6-week loading plan. (COACH-ANSWER PER-01; GEN-02 (intake))

R2 12-week cycle = 2-4 weeks acclimation ('getting used to the movements') -> 4-6 weeks driving hard, not all the way to the top -> last weeks hardest (more tired, more stimulus). Default split 3 / 6 / 3 weeks; L1 or returning 4 / 5 / 3; L3 2 / 6 / 4 (so the drive stays inside his '4 to 6 weeks'). (COACH-ANSWER PER-01; split PROPOSED)

R3 8-week plan = 'a program that wants to modify you, so you have to start hard': start about 10 % above the level start, weeks 1-4 adapting, weeks 5-8 driving hard. (COACH-ANSWER PER-01; +10 % PROPOSED)

R4 4-6-week blocks are maintenance/transition (vacation 1-2 weeks, travel, moving, off-season -> in-season, planned maintenance) at about 50-70 % of the volume, to recover and not push. (COACH-ANSWER PER-01; SCIENCE (Bickel 2011, Bosquet 2013, Ogasawara 2013))
R5 Repeated 12-week cycles start one level higher ('start at a 2 and end at an 11'): next start = previous start x 1.05, cap + 1 set. (COACH-ANSWER PER-01; step size PROPOSED)

R6 Volume moves by the person, not by muscle size: each week 3, 5 or 7 % of each muscle's weekly sets, chosen from fatigue, life and response; 10 %/week is too much; fractions are banked and released as whole sets on the first exercise of the day first. (COACH-ANSWER VOL-04, VOL-05, UNI-05, VOL-06, VOL-07)

R7 Smooth weekly increases for hypertrophy and general clients; 2-week steps and waves for fight or competition prep; the confirmed strength %-template (80/80/85/85/90/90 %, RPE 7 -> 10; Olympic 75 -> 90 % in 4 weeks) is the step pattern for main lifts. (COACH-ANSWER PER-10, PER-09)

R8 Blocks of 4-6 weeks: same exercises inside a block, 1-2 small variable changes at the next block; A/B lead-lift weeks only for clients who want variety; the second weekly exposure of a slot is a different exercise and only one axial-loading day a week. (COACH-ANSWER PER-02, PER-03, PER-04)

R9 Deload = about half the sets, same exercises, lighter or 3+ RIR, no buy-outs or finishers. Not planned at a fixed week: triggered by the logs, used as week 1 of the next cycle, or replaced by a maintenance block. (COACH-ANSWER PER-05; placement PROPOSED)
R10 A slot moves up a level at the end of a block when it felt '8 - That was perfect' or easier with no pain. (COACH-ANSWER PER-06)
R11 Tests are chosen by checkbox at the start of a block (or 'No need for testing'); the plan schedules them at the end of the block and reminds the client. (COACH-ANSWER PER-07)

R12 Athletes: off-season most volume (VOL 1 -> VOL 2 -> VOL 3, one per block; STARTING/MID/ADVANCED as blocks or levels by need); pre-season more speed/power, less volume; in-season 2 days, low volume, minimal bilateral; post-season recovery. (COACH-ANSWER PER-08, PER-11, PRG-04, UNI-10)
R13 Effort is written in RIR, 1-3 RIR at all times; 'MAX' only on small-muscle or bodyweight work; the hardest weeks sit at 1 RIR. (COACH-ANSWER VOL-13, GEN-08; ramp PROPOSED)

R14 Athletic work has its own budget (never muscle sets): programs start ballistic and become plyometric through receive & pause -> receive then create -> repeated stages; everyone in athletic training gets an Olympic-lift variant. (COACH-ANSWER VOL-10, CAT-10, CAT-11, ATH-10)
R15 The plan adjusts week to week from logged EFFORT and HOW IT FELT (pain -> swap or cut; EFFORT 9-10 -> hold or cut; EFFORT <= 6 -> add). (COACH-ANSWER GEN-05)

deload_test_taper_rules.rule: 12-week cycle: no deload at a fixed week. A deload happens when the logs trigger it (D6), and the first week of the NEXT cycle is a deload (skip it when a maintenance block came between).
deload_test_taper_rules.evidence: PER-01 rejected 'weeks 1-6 + week-7 deload + 5'; his 12-week description has no deload; SCIENCE: Bell 2023 Delphi (deload can sit in the last week of a block or the first week of the next; planned or autoregulated), Rogerson 2024 survey (every 5.6 +/- 2.3 weeks)
deload_test_taper_rules.v0: weeks 1-6 load, week 7 MID DELOAD, weeks 8-12 load (OBSERVED in STRENGTH-12 / AESTHETICS-12)

deload_test_taper_rules.rule: 8-week plan: no planned deload inside (it 'starts hard' and drives weeks 5-8); triggered deloads only; the next plan opens with a deload or a maintenance block.
deload_test_taper_rules.evidence: PER-01 8-week description; observed 8-week products end in 'DELOAD WEEK' (AESTHETICS-8 L35), 'TEST'/'DELOAD' (STRENGTH-8 L9:L21) or a peak (BOXING J col)
deload_test_taper_rules.v0: weeks 1-7 load, week 8 deload or test

deload_test_taper_rules.rule: A 4-6-week maintenance/transition block replaces loading when life needs it: vacation (1-2 weeks inside it), travel, moving, season change (off -> in), or planned maintenance. Volume about 50-70 % of the last block (50 % vacation/limited equipment, 60 % travel/moving/season change, 70 % planned maintenance; older adults >= 70 %), rate 0, RIR 2-3, no intensifiers; keep the loads, cut the sets.
deload_test_taper_rules.evidence: Coach answer text; SCIENCE: Bickel 2011 (1/3 of the dose kept size in young adults; older adults needed more), Spiering 2021, Bosquet 2013 (strength stable up to ~4 weeks without training; faster losses in 65+), Ogasawara 2013 (3-week breaks between 6-week blocks did not reduce 24-week hypertrophy)
deload_test_taper_rules.status: COACH-ANSWER PER-01; factor split, base and older floor PROPOSED

deload_test_taper_rules.rule: Vacation of 1-2 weeks: train at ~50 % with what is available (bodyweight, hotel gym), or rest completely; return at the previous start (no opening deload, no level step).
deload_test_taper_rules.evidence: Coach mentions 'a vacation 1-week or vacation 2-week kind of thing'; SCIENCE Bosquet 2013 (maximal strength mostly unaffected up to ~28 days off), Ogasawara 2013

deload_test_taper_rules.rule: Early (unplanned) deload when: 2 weeks of hold in a row; median EFFORT >= 9 two weeks in a row; 'Felt a PAIN' on 2+ slots in one week; or performance down on 3+ main lifts for 2 exposures. After it, resume at the volume of 2 weeks before.
deload_test_taper_rules.evidence: BYOP EFFORT / HOW IT FELT? menus (MASTER EXERCISE LIBRARY AX8:AY17); 12_volume_algorithm_v1 §3.7, §3.12
deload_test_taper_rules.status: COACH-ANSWER GEN-05 (adjust from logs); triggers PROPOSED
deload_test_taper_rules.v0: D11 (EFFORT 9-10 two weeks; pain on 2+ exercises; load/reps falling 2 sessions)

deload_test_taper_rules.rule: Tests are chosen by checkbox at the start of the block, or 'No need for testing'. The test day sits in the last week of the block and replaces that week's top sets; the rest of that week runs at about 50-70 % of its sets. Reminders before the test (section 6.1).
deload_test_taper_rules.evidence: Coach answer text ('they can check those boxes at the beginning...'); observed test items: 'LVL 5 = Work up to 1RM' (CF R25), STRENGTH-8 'TEST' (L9/L13), CARDIO 'DISTANCE TEST'/'SPEED TEST', '5/10/05' and 'LEFT TEST' (COD list); SCIENCE Pritchard 2016 (powerlifters cut volume ~59 % before a meet and keep intensity)
deload_test_taper_rules.status: COACH-ANSWER PER-07; test-week dose and reminder schedule PROPOSED
deload_test_taper_rules.v0: D9 (strength/aerobic/athletic test items; test-week content INFERRED)

deload_test_taper_rules.rule: Before a season opener, event or fight: 1-2 weeks, volume -40-60 % (progressive), intensity and frequency kept, no new exercises.
deload_test_taper_rules.evidence: BASEBALL Block 2 ends with 'DELOAD WEEK' right before Block 3; SCIENCE Bosquet 2007, Pritchard 2016, Vachon 2020 (team sports)
deload_test_taper_rules.status: OBSERVED shape + SCIENCE dose; COACH-ANSWER PER-08 (pre-season: less volume, more speed/power)

deload_test_taper_rules.rule: Post-season / end of a throwing block: a recovery week that is not a scaled copy (arm care, mobility, easy aerobic, no main lifts), then general work before the next off-season.
deload_test_taper_rules.evidence: BASEBALL Block 1 'wk 8': 'Kettlebell arm bars' 3 x '10/10', 'Half kneeling shoulder roll' 3 x '8/8', 'Paced Cardio - easy' 4 x '10 min'
deload_test_taper_rules.status: OBSERVED; COACH-ANSWER PER-08 ('post-season: recovery and general work')

deload_test_taper_rules.rule: Yearly mode: the last 2 weeks of December switch automatically to maintenance (about 50-70 %; default 60 %), any equipment, RIR 2-3; January restarts at the previous start.
deload_test_taper_rules.evidence: Coach answer text ('The last couple of weeks of the year, for New Year's and Christmas, it just automatically puts you in maintenance'); SCIENCE Yanovski 2000, Diaz-Zavala 2017 (holiday weight gain is small but tends to persist)

deload_test_taper_rules.rule: In-season: no planned deload; rate 0; a lighter week around congested game/travel weeks.
deload_test_taper_rules.evidence: BASEBALL Block 3 has no deload (OBSERVED)
deload_test_taper_rules.status: COACH-ANSWER PER-08 (low volume); lighter week INFERRED

deload_test_taper_rules.rule: After a productive 12-week cycle the next one starts one level higher (start x 1.05, cap + 1 set; max 25 non-priority, 30 priority). After holds, pain or a maintenance block: same start.
deload_test_taper_rules.evidence: Coach: 'you might want to start at a 2 and end at an 11'; 12_volume_algorithm_v1 §3.12 cycles

autoregulation.signal: Median weekly EFFORT >= 9 ('9 - That was terrible') or '10 - I'm done' on 2+ exercises
autoregulation.action: HOLD: rate 0 % for everyone next week
autoregulation.tag: COACH-ANSWER GEN-05 ('EFFORT 9-10 -> hold or cut sets')

autoregulation.signal: Median weekly EFFORT <= 6 ('6 - Broke a Sweat' or easier)
autoregulation.action: ADD: at least 5 %, and raise load or reps first

autoregulation.signal: EFFORT 7-8 ('7 - That was tough' / '8 - That was perfect') with sessions done
autoregulation.action: rate from the readiness score R = 0.40 effort + 0.20 completion + 0.20 performance + 0.20 life: >= 85 -> 7 %, 70-84 -> 5 %, 55-69 -> 3 %, < 55 -> hold
autoregulation.tag: COACH-ANSWER VOL-05 (by the person); score PROPOSED (12_volume_algorithm_v1 §3.7)

autoregulation.action: next exposure: swap inside the category to a more constrained, split-grip or unilateral variant, keep the sets if possible; again -> that slot -30-50 %, muscle rate 0; a third time -> drop the exercise for the block and flag for the coach

autoregulation.signal: HOW IT FELT? 'Felt the WRONG muscle'
autoregulation.action: change one variable inside the same category; volume unchanged
regress one exercise level or use an assisted version; volume unchanged

autoregulation.signal: HOW IT FELT? 'Felt the RIGHT muscles' + '8 - That was perfect' or easier through the block, no pain
autoregulation.action: slot moves up one level at the next block

autoregulation.signal: 2 weeks of hold in a row, or the D6 triggers
autoregulation.action: deload next week (about half the sets)
the whole plan uses the intake rate (default 5 %; 3 % if stressed, older, returning or in pain; never 7 % before logs)

generator_pseudocode:
generate_plan(client):                                   # v1 (coach answers applied)
  level  = level_from_experience(years, months_off, ex_pro)   # L1/L2/L3 (PRG-05)
  family = map_goal(goal)       # HYPERTROPHY | STRENGTH | FAT_LOSS | GENERAL | HYBRID | ATHLETE (sport, position, season)
  mode   = client.plan_mode     # C12 | C8 | MAINT(4-6, reason) | WBW | YEAR | PREP(date) | SEASON   (PER-01, PER-08, PER-10)
  output = client.output_mode   # static | adaptive (PROPOSED: GEN-03 vs GEN-05)
  tests  = client.test_ticks    # strength / cardio / speed / jumps / body, or 'No need for testing' (PER-07)

  grid    = MODE_GRID[mode](level)            # week -> phase (ACCLIMATION/ADAPT, DRIVE, HARDEST, MAINTAIN, DELOAD, TEST), rate cap, RIR band, block number
  overlay = FAMILY_OVERLAY[family]            # phase -> reps, effort, load, methods, laterality, conditioning, athletic stage
  targets = volume_engine_v1.start(level, family, season, priorities, pain)   # 12_volume_algorithm_v1 §3.3-3.6
  if mode == C8:    targets *= 1.10                                           # 'start hard' (PROPOSED size)
  if mode == MAINT: targets = factor(reason, age) * mean(last_block[-4:])     # 50-70 % (PER-01)
  if previous_cycle == 'productive': start *= 1.05; cap += 1                  # 'start at a 2, end at an 11'

  week_1 = build_sessions(targets, template(family, days, minutes))  # core first; hip+push / knee+pull; one axial day; 5-7 exercises (10-12 field athletes)
  for week in grid:
      if week.role == DELOAD: emit(half_sets(previous_week)); continue        # PER-05
      rate = min(week.rate_cap, plan_rate if output == static else readiness_rate(logs))   # VOL-05, GEN-05; person total < 10 %/week (UNI-05), stagger releases (PROPOSED)
      if mode == PREP or (family == STRENGTH and lift is main): apply_steps(week)          # PER-10, PER-09
      else: bank_and_place(rate)                                                       # VOL-06, VOL-07
      apply overlay[week.phase] -> reps, RIR, %, methods (MYO last isolation; supersets as fatigue tool; contrast off-season int+)
      athletic block (own budget, VOL-10): plyo:ballistic share by sport, method stage 1 -> 2 -> 3, Olympic variant by level
      if week.block_boundary: change 1-2 small variables; rebalance bilateral share; level-up eligible slots   # PER-02, PER-06, UNI-02
      if week.is_last and tests: schedule test day, cut the rest of that week, send reminders                # PER-07
      if triggers(logs): next week = DELOAD                                                                 # D6
  after the plan: deload week 1 of next cycle | maintenance block | yearly next quarter

science.claim: Concentrated blocks: accumulation -> transmutation -> realization; residual training effects ~30 +/- 5 days for aerobic endurance and maximal strength, ~18 days anaerobic glycolytic, ~5 +/- 3 days explosive/speed qualities.
science.citation: Issurin VB. New horizons for the methodology and physiology of training periodization. Sports Med 2010;40(3):189-206 (summary source: Sportlyzer Academy 'Block Periodization')
science.maps_to: CROSSFIT macro (RES -> STR -> POW -> TEST); athlete OFF_12 (base/conversion -> intensification -> realization); short residuals for speed/power explain why the coach keeps plyos/throws in EVERY phase including in-season. v1: block durations accumulation 2-6 weeks, transmutation 2-4 fit his 4-week athlete blocks (VOL 1 -> 2 -> 3, PER-11).

science.claim: More weekly sets -> more hypertrophy with diminishing returns; counting indirect sets as 0.5 ('fractional') predicts outcomes best; strength shows stronger diminishing returns and benefits more from frequency.
science.citation: Pelland JC et al. The Resistance Training Dose Response: Meta-Regressions Exploring the Effects of Weekly Volume and Frequency on Muscle Hypertrophy and Strength Gains. Sports Med 2026;56(2):481-505 (online 2025).
science.maps_to: v1 counts helpers at 0.25 (COACH-ANSWER VOL-09); Pelland's 0.5 is stored for research comparison (12_volume_algorithm_v1); 15-20 / 20-25 bands (UNI-01).

science.claim: Graded dose-response: each additional weekly set ~ +0.37 % gain; 10+ sets/muscle/week trend best.
science.citation: Schoenfeld BJ, Ogborn D, Krieger JW. Dose-response relationship between weekly resistance training volume and increases in muscle mass. J Sports Sci 2017.
science.maps_to: floors (>= ~10 sets for growth muscles).

science.claim: 12-20 weekly sets per muscle may be an optimum standard; >20 not clearly better for quads/biceps (triceps responded to higher).
science.citation: Baz-Valle E et al. A Systematic Review of The Effects of Different Resistance Training Volumes on Muscle Hypertrophy. J Hum Kinet 2022.
science.maps_to: the coach's 15-20 band (UNI-01) sits inside 12-20; his 20-25 'growth' range is where only triceps showed extra benefit (12_volume_algorithm_v1 §2.2); level caps L2 22 / L3 25 (PROPOSED).

science.claim: Hypertrophy improves as sets end closer to failure; strength gains similar across a wide RIR range.
science.citation: Robinson ZP et al. Exploring the Dose-Response Relationship Between Estimated Resistance Training Proximity to Failure, Strength Gain, and Muscle Hypertrophy. Sports Med 2024.
science.maps_to: isolation 'MAX'/'ALL', compounds 1-2 RIR; strength waves can stay at RPE 7-9.

science.topic: Progressive overload by load or reps
science.claim: Progressing repetitions at a fixed load produced hypertrophy and strength similar to progressing load in trained lifters.
science.citation: Plotkin D et al. Progressive overload without progressing load? PeerJ 2022; also Chaves TS et al. Int J Sports Med 2024.
science.maps_to: supports progressing small-muscle work by reps (VOL-11: small muscles 12-30); 40-rep sets stay an AMRAP option only (VOL-11); the study used lower-body exercises, so it supports rep progression in general.

science.claim: Heavier loads (>80 %) maximise strength; multi-set prescriptions rank highest for hypertrophy; all loads build muscle.
science.citation: Currier BS et al. Resistance training prescription for muscle strength and hypertrophy in healthy adults: a systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis. Br J Sports Med 2023.
science.maps_to: strength family drives % to 80-95 %; hypertrophy family drives sets.

science.claim: Volume-equated: periodized > non-periodized for 1RM; undulating slightly better for strength in trained people; no hypertrophy difference.
science.citation: Moesgaard L et al. Effects of Periodization on Strength and Muscle Hypertrophy in Volume-Equated Resistance Training Programs: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis. Sports Med 2022.
science.maps_to: the coach's within-week undulation (BASEBALL speed/strength days; FAT BURN heavy Tue / light Fri; leg ext '6 & 6' Mon vs '20/20' Thu) is supported for strength; hypertrophy depends on volume, not the scheme.

science.claim: Best taper: ~2 weeks, volume reduced 41-60 % (progressive/exponential), intensity and frequency maintained.
science.citation: Bosquet L et al. Effects of tapering on performance: a meta-analysis. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2007; Wang Z et al. PLOS ONE 2023; Mujika I, Padilla S. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2003; Vachon A et al. Eur J Sport Sci 2020 (team sports: taper improves power, RSA, COD, VO2max).
science.maps_to: deload/taper depth: his v1 deload (about half the sets, PER-05) sits inside the 41-60 % taper range; pre-season ends with a taper (D8).

science.claim: Expert consensus: deload = period of reduced training stress to mitigate fatigue; commonly 5-7 days every 4-6 weeks, highly variable; usually cut volume more than intensity.
science.citation: Bell L et al. Integrating Deloading into Strength and Physique Sports Training Programmes: An International Delphi Consensus Approach. Sports Med Open 2023 (definition); Bell L, Nolan D, Immonen V, et al. Front Sports Act Living 2022, qualitative interviews with 18 strength/physique coaches (deloads typically every 4-6 weeks, about 1 week long; range from every few weeks to 6-12 weeks).
science.maps_to: v1: deload = about half the sets (PER-05); placement by triggers or week 1 of the next cycle (PROPOSED); deloads every 4-6(7) weeks in practice (open question on his 12-week shape).

science.claim: MEV -> MAV -> MRV; mesocycles of 4-6 weeks start near MEV, add sets weekly, deload at ~50 % volume when MRV is reached. Landmarks from RP's own muscle guides (practitioner, not peer-reviewed; intermediate lifters): chest MEV 4-6 / MAV 6-16 / MRV 16-24; quads 4-6 / 6-14 / 14-18; biceps 8-10 / 14-20 / 20-26; triceps 4-6 / 6-16 / 16-20; calves 4-6 / 6-16 / 16-24; specialisation (MRV*P) up to 24-35. Back values are published only as an image and were not extracted.
science.citation: Israetel M et al. (Renaissance Periodization) muscle training-tips guides at rpstrength.com (chest, quad, biceps, triceps, calves); framework summary at arvo.guru (which gives no per-muscle numbers).
science.maps_to: v1: his 12-week shape (acclimation -> drive -> hardest, then deload or maintenance) is the RP mesocycle logic; RP adds ~1 set/muscle/week, his person-level 3/5/7 % adds ~0.5-1.1 set/week at 15-20 sets (12_volume_algorithm_v1 §2.5); the v0 'INFERRED governor' comparison is retired.

science.claim: Strength/size maintained for up to 32 weeks with as little as 1 session/week and 1 set/exercise if relative load (intensity) is maintained; 1 strength session/week maintained strength, sprint and jump in pro soccer for 12 weeks, every second week did not.
science.citation: Spiering BA et al. J Strength Cond Res 2021; Ronnestad BR et al. J Strength Cond Res 2011; Cuthbert M et al. Sports Med 2021 (frequency can be distributed in-season).
science.maps_to: v1: in-season 2 days/week, low volume, keep intensity (COACH-ANSWER PER-08, UNI-10) now agrees with this evidence.

science.claim: Aerobic + strength does not blunt hypertrophy or maximal strength, but explosive strength gains are attenuated, mostly when both are in the same session.
science.citation: Schumann M et al. Compatibility of Concurrent Aerobic and Strength Training for Skeletal Muscle Size and Function: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. Sports Med 2021.
science.maps_to: coach puts steady cardio on separate days (Wed/Sat) and short buy-outs at the END of sessions; CROSSFIT power months drop strength/resistance.

science.claim: Complex training improves sprint (5-20 m), COD and CMJ more than resistance training alone (low certainty); French contrast meta: large sprint and moderate jump effects, not max strength; >= 7-8 weeks and ~3 sessions/week optimise effects.
science.citation: Thapa RK et al. J Sports Sci 2024; Cormier P et al. J Strength Cond Res 2020; Zhao ZR et al. Front Physiol 2025.
science.maps_to: v1: contrast / French contrast and complexes for intermediate+ athletes in the off-season only (COACH-ANSWER ATH-12), so they sit in the off-season drive and hardest blocks (8.2.2), not pre-season.

science.claim: Common guideline: ~80-100 foot contacts/session beginner, 100-120 intermediate, 120-140 advanced (off-season). The PMC7873906 table is a study protocol (72 -> 126 contacts/session over 8 weeks in female basketball players, judged insufficient by its authors), not a ceiling; no source here supports a 200/400-contacts-per-session limit.
science.citation: NSCA Essentials (CSCS ch. 18) guideline as summarised by PT Pioneer; PMC7873906 (female basketball plyometric study, table 3).
science.maps_to: the coach's weekly contacts (32-324/week) sit well below per-session ceilings because plyos are spread over 2-4 short primers; low-amplitude reactive contacts can be much higher (squirrel jumps, rope).

science.claim: Acute:chronic workload ratio 0.8-1.3 described as a 'sweet spot'; spikes >1.5 associated with injury in team sports (the ratio is methodologically debated).
science.citation: Gabbett TJ. Br J Sports Med 2016 (summarised by Catapult / Vitruve).
science.maps_to: guardrail on week-to-week contact/sprint increases (<= ~10-15 %); the coach's 3/5/7 % is far inside it, his +41 % boxing wk3 jump is a phase change from 0 that should be preceded by base work.

science.claim: Max-effort (90-100 %) and dynamic-effort (Westside: roughly 50-60 % bar weight plus ~25 % band/chain tension, moved fast) days in the same week, rotating ME exercises every 1-3 weeks, with repeated-effort accessories.
science.citation: Westside Barbell 'Conjugate Method' (practitioner source); Zatsiorsky & Kraemer, Science and Practice of Strength Training.
science.maps_to: STRENGTH-8 is conjugate in structure ('conjugate style training') but the coach adds his own grammar (the work / accessory / nuance / survival; KD-HD alternation; plyo row labelled 'the work' on the speed day in the CONJUGATE draft). v1: 'I don't need it to be conjugate' (PER-01); band/chain tension out of scope (EQ-12).

science.claim: 13 studies: linear and daily undulating periodization gave similar muscle growth (d = -0.02, 95 % CI -0.25 to 0.21).
science.citation: Grgic J, Mikulic P, Podnar H, Pedisic Z. Effects of linear and daily undulating periodized resistance training programs on measures of muscle hypertrophy: a systematic review and meta-analysis. PeerJ 2017;5:e3695.
science.maps_to: Smooth weekly increases for hypertrophy (PER-10) are as good as fancier schemes; volume and effort matter more than the model. Supports the simple 12-week shape.

science.claim: 17 studies, 510 people: no difference between linear and undulating periodization for upper- or lower-body strength.
science.citation: Harries SK, Lubans DR, Callister R. Systematic review and meta-analysis of linear and undulating periodized resistance training programs on muscular strength. J Strength Cond Res 2015;29(4).
science.maps_to: The confirmed 2-week %-steps for strength (PER-09) are a valid choice, not the only one; the generator can keep his template.

science.claim: 18 studies: periodized plans improved 1RM more than non-periodized plans (ES 0.43); undulating programs and higher frequency/longer studies favoured larger gains.
science.citation: Williams TD, Tolusso DV, Fedewa MV, Esco MR. Comparison of periodized and non-periodized resistance training on maximal strength: a meta-analysis. Sports Med 2017;47(10).
science.maps_to: Planned variation between blocks (PER-02) and planned phases (PER-01) are worth having for strength; the shape itself is less important than having one.

science.claim: 10 weeks in Division I track and field athletes: no significant difference; block training produced similar strength with less volume (higher 'efficiency').
science.citation: Painter KB et al. Strength gains: block versus daily undulating periodization weight training among track and field athletes. Int J Sports Physiol Perform 2012;7(2).
science.maps_to: Athlete off-season blocks (VOL 1 -> 2 -> 3, PER-11) are a sound way to organise athletes.

science.topic: Early weeks of a new program
science.claim: Muscle damage is highest in week 1, lower by week 3 and minimal by week 10; protein synthesis tracks muscle growth only once damage has dropped (weeks 3 and 10, not week 1).
science.citation: Damas F et al. Resistance training-induced changes in integrated myofibrillar protein synthesis are related to hypertrophy only after attenuation of muscle damage. J Physiol 2016;594(18):5209-5222.
science.maps_to: Grounds his 2-4 'getting used to the movements' weeks: early volume mostly pays for repair, so the acclimation rate is kept low (<= 3 %).

science.claim: A first exposure to a new exercise protects against damage on later bouts; protection can last weeks to months and can be induced by submaximal or small doses.
science.citation: Nosaka K, Aoki MS. Repeated bout effect: research update and future perspective. Brazilian J Biomotricity 2011; McHugh MP. Recent advances in the understanding of the repeated bout effect. Scand J Med Sci Sports 2003.
science.maps_to: Supports a gentle acclimation and supports the 8-week plan 'starting hard' for people coming straight from training (already protected); after a layoff, use the 12-week acclimation.

science.claim: Three 6-week training blocks separated by 3-week breaks gave similar muscle growth to 24 weeks of continuous training; growth rate after each break returned to the early-training rate.
science.citation: Ogasawara R, Yasuda T, Ishii N, Abe T. Comparison of muscle hypertrophy following 6-month of continuous and periodic strength training. Eur J Appl Physiol 2013.
science.maps_to: Maintenance/vacation blocks and repeated cycles do not cost long-term growth (PER-01); returning at the previous start after a maintenance block is safe.

science.claim: Meta-analysis of 103 studies: strength losses grow with time off; maximal strength was mostly unaffected for up to ~4 weeks (trivial effects), losses accelerate after that and are larger in people over 65 and in inactive people.
science.citation: Bosquet L et al. Effect of training cessation on muscular performance: a meta-analysis. Scand J Med Sci Sports 2013 (summary: Stronger by Science, 'Detraining').
science.maps_to: A 1-2-week vacation (PER-01) costs little; older clients keep the high end of maintenance (>= 70 %).

science.claim: Resistance training in an energy deficit (RCTs of 3+ weeks) blunted lean-mass gains; in the meta-regression a deficit of about 500 kcal/day predicted no lean-mass gain on average, while strength gains were not impaired.
science.citation: Murphy C, Koehler K. Energy deficiency impairs resistance training gains in lean mass but not strength: a meta-analysis and meta-regression. Scand J Med Sci Sports 2022.
science.maps_to: Fat-loss plans and the yearly Q1 cut hold volume near the level start (rate <= 3 %) and keep loads heavy; growth volume belongs to Q4 (PROPOSED).

science.claim: Adults gain about 0.4-0.9 kg over the holiday season; the gain is small but is usually not lost later and is a large share of yearly weight gain.
science.citation: Yanovski JA et al. A prospective study of holiday weight gain. N Engl J Med 2000; Diaz-Zavala RG et al. Effect of the holiday season on weight gain: a narrative review. J Obes 2017.
science.maps_to: Automatic holiday maintenance (PER-01) keeps the habit going at low volume instead of stopping.

science.claim: Eleven elite raw powerlifters (interviews) peaked volume 5.2 +/- 1.7 weeks and intensity 1.9 +/- 0.8 weeks before competition, cut volume by 58.9 +/- 8.4 % in the taper while keeping intensity, and trained last 3.7 +/- 1.6 days out.
science.citation: Pritchard HJ et al. Tapering practices of New Zealand's elite raw powerlifters. J Strength Cond Res 2016;30(7).
science.maps_to: Test week: reduce the rest of that week's volume and keep load (PER-07, PROPOSED dose); strength 'hardest' weeks peak intensity, not volume.

science.claim: Survey of 246 strength and physique athletes: deload every 5.6 +/- 2.3 weeks for 6.4 +/- 1.7 days, 79 % cut sets; a 1-week break in the middle of a 9-week program did not change growth and slightly reduced strength gains.
science.citation: Rogerson D, Bell L et al. Sports Med Open 2024; Coleman M et al. PeerJ 2024 (carried from 12_volume_algorithm_v1 §2.7).
science.maps_to: Most lifters deload more often than once per 12 weeks: the triggered deload (D6) will fire for many clients; the 'half the sets' dose (PER-05) matches practice.

science.claim: After 16 weeks of training, 1/3 of the dose kept (and in young adults slightly grew) muscle size for 32 weeks; 1/9 kept size in the young; older adults needed more.
science.citation: Bickel CS, Cross JM, Bamman MM. Exercise dosing to retain resistance training adaptations in young and older adults. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2011 (carried from 12_volume_algorithm_v1 §2.4).
science.maps_to: His 50-70 % maintenance volume is well above the minimum; older clients >= 70 % (PER-01, PROPOSED floor).

science.claim: Classic periodization models rest on tradition more than evidence; responses vary widely between people, so plans should be responsive systems that adjust to the individual. A review of 42 periodization trials found mostly short studies of strength only, none longer than about 9 months, and individual responses ignored.
science.citation: Kiely J. Periodization paradigms in the 21st century: evidence-led or tradition-driven? Int J Sports Physiol Perform 2012;7(3):242-250; Afonso J et al. Is empirical research on periodization trustworthy? J Sports Sci Med 2017.
science.maps_to: Supports the week-by-week mode and the readiness-based rate (GEN-05, VOL-05): the 12-week shape is a default, the logs steer it.

science.claim: Practitioner models describe three ways to raise loads: straight-line, stepped (a jump then a hold) and wave-like (rise, then a lighter microcycle); the stepped method lets athletes master higher loads (Bompa).
science.citation: Bompa TO. Theory and Methodology of Training (stepped vs rectilinear vs wave loading), summarised by Stadion Books.
science.maps_to: Steps and waves for fight/competition prep (PER-10). No controlled study shows steps beat smooth increases for hypertrophy (see SCI_LP_DUP_HYP), so smooth stays the default for hypertrophy/general.

science.claim: After 20 weeks off, size returned to baseline but about 60 % of the strength gain remained (motor learning); older men regained their 1RM in under 8 weeks after 12 weeks off; regaining lost size and strength usually takes about half as long as the time off.
science.citation: Psilander N et al. Effects of training, detraining, and retraining on strength, hypertrophy, and myonuclear number in human skeletal muscle. J Appl Physiol 2019; Blocquiaux S et al. The effect of resistance training, detraining and retraining on muscle strength and power, myofibre size, satellite cells and myonuclei in older men. Exp Gerontol 2020; summary: Stronger by Science 'Detraining'.
science.maps_to: His layoff rule (PRG-05): after 6-12+ months off the body is treated as a beginner (L1 volume) while skills come back fast (exercise level kept); ex-pros stay at L1 only briefly. The 12-week acclimation (4 weeks for returning clients) fits.

science.claim: Resistance-trained men kept their leg-press strength and lean mass after 2 weeks of detraining.
science.citation: Hwang PS et al. Resistance training-induced elevations in muscular strength in trained men are maintained after 2 weeks of detraining and not differentially affected by whey protein supplementation. J Strength Cond Res 2017.
science.maps_to: A 1-2-week vacation (PER-01) inside a maintenance block costs little: ~50 % with what is available, or full rest, then return at the previous start (D5, PROPOSED).

science.claim: Common power guidance: multiple-effort power work at 75-85 % 1RM for 3-5 reps per set, single-effort at 80-90 % for 1-2 reps, 3-5 sets with 2-5 min rest; pulling derivatives (no catch) allow heavier loads and similar or greater force and velocity than catch variants.
science.citation: NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning, power load assignment (summary); Suchomel TJ, Comfort P, Lake JP. Enhancing the force-velocity profile of athletes using weightlifting derivatives. Strength Cond J 2017.
science.maps_to: Science check he asked for in PER-09: his 4 x 6 @ 80-85 % and 4 x 4 @ 90 % sit close to this guidance; 4 x 8 @ 75 % is more reps per set than usual for full catch lifts (technique fades late in long sets). Fine for DB/KB and hang-pull variants; for full lifts a 3-5-rep option is PROPOSED (round-2 question).

open_questions: Yearly mode (PER-01): (a) you said 'this second half of the year, the second quarter'; we read Q2 = April-June, right? (b) Is Q2 a fat-loss quarter continuing Q1's cut, or a lean-gain quarter ('build a little more muscle and keep fat down')? Which quarter carries the main cut? (c) Is Q3 'maintain' the 50-70 % maintenance volume or your 15-20-set 'maintenance to a little growth' band? (d) In the Q1 cut, should volume still step up a level, or hold while the extra work comes from cardio?

Yearly calendar: fixed months (northern-hemisphere summer, Christmas/New Year) or the user's own summer, event date and holidays (southern-hemisphere users, Semana Santa, Thanksgiving, personal vacations)? Should athletes in yearly mode follow their season calendar instead of quarters?

Deloads in your 12-week shape: you rejected the week-7 mid deload, yet STRENGTH-12 ('MID DELOAD') and AESTHETICS-12 ('A WEEK LOWER') both have one. Planned at a fixed week, only when the person needs it, or as week 1 of the next cycle?

Season change: PER-01 lists 'transitioning from off-season to on-season' as a 4-6-week maintenance use, and PER-08 describes pre-season as less volume, more speed/power. Is pre-season that same block (maintenance-level lifting + speed/power), or are they separate?

'12/10/8 -20' (PRG-07): the light 20 is an extra set. In AESTHETICS-12 the SETS row says 3 next to '12/10/8 -20' (weeks 1-3) but 4 next to '12/12/10-20' (weeks 4-6). Does the light 20 count inside SETS or on top, and does it count as a hard set?

In-season Olympic lifts: ATH-10 says everyone in athletic training gets Olympic lifts, but BASEBALL Block 3 (in-season) has none and PER-08 says in-season = sprints, strength maintenance or jumps. Keep a light Olympic/power piece in-season, or none?

Contrast/complexes are off-season only (ATH-12), but the BASEBALL Block 2 complexes ('5 of each') sit in a block we had read as pre-season. Is Block 2 late off-season (VOL 3), and do complexes stop when pre-season begins? The same question for fight camps: your 'EXAMPLE BOXING 8 WEEK BUILD UP' uses complexes from week 3, and we use it as the fight-prep pattern (PER-10). Does a fight camp count as 'off-season' for complexes, or should a camp drop them?

'Start at a 2 and end at an 11' for advanced clients already at the 25-set ceiling: should 'one level higher' then mean heavier loads and intensifiers, rotating priority muscles (cap ~30), or a personal cap learned from their logs?

PRG-04 ('depends on whatever is needed'): proposed rule = an off-season of 16+ weeks for an L1-L2 athlete runs STARTING -> MID -> ADVANCED as consecutive blocks; a shorter off-season or an L3 athlete gets the template that matches their level. OK?

Olympic ramp (PER-09, you asked us to make sure it is correct): 4 x 6 @ 80-85 % and 4 x 4 @ 90 % match common power guidance, but 4 x 8 @ 75 % is more reps per set than usual for full catch lifts (squat clean, squat snatch), where technique fades late in a set. Keep 8s for DB/KB and hang-pull/hang-power variants and use 3-5-rep sets for the full lifts (same weekly reps), or keep 4 x 8 for everything? And is the % taken from the 1RM of that exact variant (hang clean, power clean)?

8-week plan (PER-01): you said 'the first 4 weeks ... getting used to it, then the next 4 weeks ... driving it hard', and also 'you want good stimulus for the last 5 weeks' and 'you have to start hard'. Is it 4 + 4 or 3 + 5? And does 'start hard' mean more weekly sets than a 12-week start (we propose +10 %), harder effort (2 RIR from week 1), or both?

Week-by-week mode (PER-01: 'just keep me in line ... and then it does it by itself') can only adjust if the person reports how the week went. You also said people should track on their own (GEN-03). Is a 30-second weekly check-in (sessions done, effort, any pain, sleep/stress) acceptable for this mode, while fixed 8- and 12-week plans can be used without any tracking?

changes.change: Plan lengths rebuilt. The v0 fixed shapes (8 weeks = 7 loading + deload/test; 12 weeks = 6 + week-7 mid deload + 5; 6 weeks = first half of the 12) are retired. v1 modes: 4-6-week maintenance/transition at about 50-70 % volume (vacation, travel, season change, moving); 8 weeks = 4 adapting + 4 driving hard, starting hard; 12 weeks (preferred) = 2-4 acclimation + 4-6 driving hard (not to the top) + hardest last weeks; repeated 12-week cycles start one level higher ('start at a 2 and end at an 11'); open-ended week-by-week mode; yearly mode with quarter themes and automatic holiday maintenance.

Deloads: the v0 fixed deload/test weeks (week 8 of 8, week 7 of 12, week 6 of 6) are retired with the shapes he rejected. Deload dose confirmed: about half the sets, same exercises, lighter load or 3+ RIR, no buy-out or finisher. Placement is PROPOSED and aligned with 12_volume_algorithm_v1 §3.12: triggered by the logs, week 1 of the next cycle, or replaced by a maintenance block.

Weekly progression = 3, 5 or 7 % of a muscle's weekly sets, chosen by the PERSON's state (fatigue, life, response), coach-adjustable; 10 %/week is too much (hard ceiling). The v0 size tiers (big 3 % / medium 5 % / small 7 %), the focus 'one tier up' rule and the v0 worked example are retired.
Rounding: bank the fraction every week and add a whole set when the bank reaches 1; the tool computes the percentages, not the client.

Where a new set goes: 3-4 exercises per muscle per day; add to the first exercise in session order, then the next (2/2/2 -> 3/2/2 -> 3/3/2 -> 3/3/3 -> 4/3/3); small muscles at the end of a session get extra volume as a bonus exercise.

Smooth weekly increases for hypertrophy and general clients; 2-week steps and waves for fight or competition prep. The v0 'STEP mode default for strength/athlete/hybrid' is retired; the confirmed strength %-template is the competition-style step pattern for main lifts.

Strength %-template confirmed (Olympic lifts 75 -> 80 -> 85 -> 90 % with 4x8 -> 4x6 -> 4x6 -> 4x4; main lift 80/80/85/85/90/90 % with RPE 7 -> 10) and placed inside the v1 12-week shape. He added 'I just want to make sure it's correct', so a science check is attached: the main-lift loads sit within about 1-4 percentage points of the RPE chart; the Olympic 4 x 8 @ 75 % is above common power guidance (3-5 reps per set at 75-85 %) for full catch lifts and is flagged for round 2.

Set counting: helpers 0.25 (not 0.5); dips 0.5 triceps / 0.5 chest; a 10/10 unilateral set = 1 set; athletic patterns (plyos, ballistics, throws, Olympic lifts, sprints) never count toward muscle volume.

Blocks are 4-6 weeks; exercises stay fixed inside a block; the next block changes 1-2 small variables (grip, stance, implement, range of motion, rep range). A/B lead-lift weeks are an option for clients who want variety, not a default.

The second exposure of a slot in a week is a different exercise from the same category, and axial spinal loading happens once a week (squat one day; leg press or belt squat the other; deadlifts load the spine too).
A slot moves up a level at the end of a block if it felt '8 - That was perfect' or easier with no pain. Exercise levels are still theoretical; do not over-rely on them.
Tests: the client or coach ticks what to test at the start of a block (strength, cardio, speed, ...) or 'No need for testing'; the plan schedules the test at the end of the block and reminds them.

Athlete seasons confirmed: off-season most volume (strength + plyos); pre-season more speed/power, less volume; in-season 2 days/week, low volume (sprints for speed athletes, strength maintenance or jumps for others; bilateral work minimal); post-season recovery and general work.
VOL 1 / VOL 2 / VOL 3 (compound 12-15 / 8-12 / 6-8 reps) = one rep phase per off-season block for every athlete.
Off-season STARTING / MID / ADVANCED: back-to-back blocks or athlete levels, 'depends on whatever is needed' (decision rule PROPOSED).

Week-to-week adjustment from logged EFFORT and HOW IT FELT confirmed; the person-level readiness rate of 12_volume_algorithm_v1 replaces the v0 per-muscle autoregulation table. The GEN-03 'they should track it themselves' conflict is handled by a static vs adaptive output mode (PROPOSED).

Effort: RIR is the model (1-3 RIR at all times, RPE explained alongside); 'MAX' = technical failure only on small-muscle or bodyweight work; never to failure on heavy compounds. A ramp inside the 1-3 RIR band across the phases is PROPOSED.
Rest: hypertrophy 1-2 min (up to 3), strength 3-6 min, athletic as prescribed.

Methods: MYO sets only on the last machine/isolation exercise; supersets are a fatigue/density tool (short time, advanced clients needing more stimulus, off-season VO2/mitochondrial work, beginners who do not fatigue); contrast / French contrast and complexes for intermediate+ athletes in the off-season only (heavy lift about 78-85 %).

No bands and no variable resistance (bands, chains, weight releasers, reverse-banded assistance) in any generator rule; banded/chained cells stay only as OBSERVED evidence. Speed lifts use straight weight ('FAST RPE6 or about 60-70%').

Plyo 'zones' are not zones: they are method stages, receive & pause -> receive then create -> repeated receive/create (name pending). Programs start more ballistic and become more plyometric; the plyo:ballistic ratio follows the sport's ground-contact time; unilateral plyos are harder than bilateral. Davidson zones (rotation biases) do not apply to plyos.

Olympic lifts for everyone in athletic training (beginners: DB/KB snatches, hex-bar jumps, hang pulls/cleans; intermediate+: full lifts; youth may lift from the floor). Full lifts are named 'Squat Snatch', 'Squat Clean', 'Squat Clean & Jerk'; push press is easier, push jerk intermediate/advanced.
Aerobic sessions per week: 3 general/fat loss, 2 athletes in-season, 4 aesthetics/bodybuilders, plus long walks after workouts; any erg works, tracked by calories, time or distance.
Core first by default (warm-up), movable by the user; about 2 core exercises; calves 3 sets every leg day; rear delts get their own sets.

Reps: small muscles 12-30, big muscles 5-15; 40-rep sets only as a CrossFit/AMRAP option (the FAT BURN 40-rep isolation ladder is not a generator default); client preference moves the reps on big compounds only; '12/10/8 -20' = pyramid 12 (mid) / 10 (heavier) / 8 (heaviest) then a light set of 20; '10/10' = per side.
Boxers/strikers: reduce (do not cut) pressing and arm volume in weeks of high punching volume.
No medball work for aesthetics/bodybuilding clients except in the warm-up; medballs never over 20 lb; throws have no levels.

Older clients: few plyos unless they ask; extra volume on constrained machines; never overhead squat, snatch, low-bar squat or depth jumps. No sex-based rules (age, foundation, goal, injuries decide).

Bilateral:unilateral share spans 90/10 to 10/90 and moves across blocks: bodybuilders/powerlifters about 50/50 at the start (contra/ipsi health work in the first 2-4 weeks) -> 80/20-90/10; field/change-of-direction athletes 80-90 % unilateral; in-season minimal bilateral; pain adjusts it.
Pairing: same pattern (squat + lunge) for high-level/aesthetics clients, cross pattern for bootcamp; hip dominant + push and knee dominant + pull for full-body and bootcamp days.

Session size: resistance-only 5-7 exercises; field athletes off-season up to 10-12 (2 core + 2-4 plyo/ballistic + 2-3 Olympic/power + 3-4 resistance); about 1.5 h (max 2 h) for athletes, bodybuilders and powerlifters, 45-60 min for general/weight loss.
Bootcamp: timed circuits 3-5 rounds x 30-50 s, 5-7 stations, 35-45 min, 3-6 sessions a week; FAT BURN circuits are finishers after lifting.
Levels L1/L2/L3 (novice = newby: under ~6-12 months; intermediate: consistent over a year; 6-12+ months off -> body treated as beginner, skills return fast; ex-pros at L1 only briefly).
CrossFit dose tables: FULL TIME = competitor, HALF TIME = class member. Half-marathon plan (Chris Hinshaw) used as-is.
'JUSTICE LEAGUE' was a marketing name: the program is the weekend-warrior athletic program (non-competitive athletic adults and youth). Renamed everywhere outside verbatim cell quotes.

Davidson zones are rotation biases (vertical = external-rotation bias; horizontal = internal-rotation bias, compressive); level reads from load position (front-loaded foundational, on the body intermediate, behind/overhead advanced; machines easier).
'camporini deadlift' and 'strap rotating in/out' are dropped from the generator (they remain as OBSERVED cell quotes).

His Q1/Q2 wording is ambiguous; calendar anchor (hemisphere, personal dates, other holidays) not decided.
Deload placement inside the 12- and 8-week shapes: none planned; triggered by the logs, or week 1 of the next cycle (12_volume_algorithm_v1 §3.12).

12-week week split (acclimation weeks 1-3, L1 1-4, L3 1-2; drive to week 9, L3 to week 8; hardest weeks 10-12, L3 9-12, so every level drives for 4-6 weeks as he said), acclimation rate <= 3 %, 8-week start x 1.10 and rate <= 5 % in weeks 1-4.
Maintenance factors by reason (50 % vacation/limited kit, 60 % travel/moving/season change, 70 % planned maintenance; older adults >= 70 %), base = mean of the last 4 loading weeks.
Repeated cycles: next start = previous start x 1.05, cap +1 (max 25 non-priority / 30 priority); same start after holds, pain or a maintenance block.
Week-by-week mode: block boundary every 4-6 weeks; deload on triggers or after 12 loading weeks at the latest; requires logs (adaptive output).
RIR ramp inside his 1-3 RIR band: acclimation 2-3, drive 1-2, hardest 1; maintenance 2-3; deload 3+.
Strength %-template placement: acclimation weeks at ~70-75 % (RPE 6-7), drive = STRENGTH-12 weeks 1-6, hardest = STRENGTH-12 weeks 10-12 doses (~90/92/95 %).
Test catalogue, test week (test day replaces the top sets; rest of that week -30-50 %), reminder schedule (block start, 7 days and 1 day before).
In-season dose: 2 sessions/week; resistance x0.4-0.5 lower / x0.3-0.4 upper; 1-2 main lifts at 3-6 reps, RIR 2-3; >= 80-90 % unilateral.
Pre-season = the 'season change' 4-6-week block at maintenance-level resistance volume with speed/power emphasis; 1-2-week taper before the opener.
PRG-04 decision rule: off-season >= 16 weeks and L1-L2 -> STARTING, MID, ADVANCED as consecutive blocks; shorter off-season or L3 -> pick the template by level.
Fat loss / cut quarter: rate <= 3 % while in a calorie deficit; Q1 holds the level start instead of stepping up.
Fight prep: 2-week steps and waves; if a fight date is set, the last 1-2 weeks taper (the observed BOXING build-up ends at a week-8 peak). v0 question 14 is still unanswered.
Name and week split of the plyo method stages: 'Receive-Create stages' RC1 (weeks 1-2), RC2 (weeks 3-5), RC3 (week 6+).

headline_rules_v0_observed: R1 Quality x level x time: a plan is a grid of qualities (resistance/hypertrophy, strength, power, aerobic, WODs/conditioning, athletic patterns, test) with a level per period; a dose table converts level -> sets x reps (CROSSFIT A10:M17 + A19:U25). OBSERVED.

R2 Default sequence inside any block that ends in a peak: hypertrophy/base -> strength -> power -> test/realization (CROSSFIT blocks; BOXING base -> conversion; BASEBALL off -> pre -> in). OBSERVED (the BASEBALL blocks are labelled only 'BLOCK 1/2/3': their season reading is INFERRED).

R3 Plan shapes: 8 weeks = 7 loading + deload/test week 8 (exceptions: BOXING ends at a peak, HYBRID-8 has no deload, CROSSFIT class week 8 = 1RM test only); 12 weeks = 6 loading + 'MID DELOAD' week 7 + 5 loading weeks (AESTHETICS-12: new menu + intensifiers; STRENGTH-12: same A/B menu restarting at the wk3-4 dose), peak week 12. OBSERVED. 6 weeks = first half of the 12-week shape. INFERRED.

R4 Volume moves in whole-set steps (+1 set per exercise every 2-3 weeks) inside rep waves; the long-run average of those steps is 4-6 %/week in the 12-week products and FAT BURN (the 8-week products that start at 2 sets run 10-17 %/week), which is read as the coach's stated 3/5/7 %. OBSERVED numbers, INFERRED reconciliation.

R5 Compound reps fall while isolation reps rise or go to 'MAX' (BASEBALL legend 'COMPOUND' vs 'SMALLER ISOLATIONS' VOL 1-3; FAT BURN leg ext/curl slot 15 -> 20 -> 40 -> 40). Big muscles progress by load/sets, small muscles by reps/effort. OBSERVED (exception: PPL side raises/rear flies/upright rows follow the compound ladder 3x15 -> 4x8).

R6 Effort words are written per row in the conjugate tabs and follow the exercise role: max-effort AND dynamic-effort lifts '1RIR', second compound 4x6 '2RIR', upper/unilateral accessory 4x8-10 'MAX', 2-3 x '8/8' finisher 'ALL', plyo 'EASY' (Mon/Wed these are the 1st-4th rows; on Thursday the plyo row comes first, so pull-ups = 3rd row '2RIR' and lunges = 4th row 'MAX'); strength waves RPE 7 -> 9/10 (STRENGTH-12); hypertrophy '1-2 RIR' (AESTHETICS-8 only); never grind main lifts to failure. OBSERVED words; the 'unilateral = MAX / isolation = ALL' class mapping is INFERRED (STRENGTH-8 'MAX' rows are pull-ups, DB bench and lunges; its 'ALL' rows are lunges and curls).

R7 Deload = same template at 3 sets per main exercise (BASEBALL 3 x 8; AESTHETICS-12 3 x '8/8/8-12'; STRENGTH-12 3 x 4 @ RPE 7), intensifiers/conditioning/Olympic lifts removed, athletic Part A 1-2 sets; volume -25 to -50 %. OBSERVED; one unified '3 x 8 @ RPE ~7' default is INFERRED.

R8 Gym clients progress by ADDING volume with level (NOVICE -> NEWBY -> INTERMEDIATE: 76 -> 90 -> 102 sets); athletes progress by CUTTING volume and raising intensity/specificity (STARTING -> MID -> ADVANCED: 89 -> 72 -> 59 component sets, ~61 -> ~54 -> ~44 written line sets; resistance flat 44 -> 44 before falling to 24; heaviest hinge 3x6 'Heavy Snatch grip DL' -> 3x1 'DEADLIFTS (1RIR)'). OBSERVED cells, counts computed.

R9 Athletes: off-season = build (new menus, 12/10/8/8, base then conversion), pre-season = intensify/potentiate (contrast, complexes, 8/6/4/4, Oly 75 -> 90 %, sets 4 -> 5, deload before opener), in-season = maintain (Part C/D frozen at 4 x 8-10, Part A 1-3 and core 2-4 sets, no Oly, no Part C compound < 8 reps, 2 alternating familiar menus, upper supersets and banded lifts kept). OBSERVED (block-to-season mapping INFERRED).

R10 Athletic work stays in every training phase: plyos and throws in off-, pre- and in-season (BASEBALL ~200 contacts and ~180 throws/week); only the zone/amplitude and the slot quality change. Exceptions: the boxer's 2 base weeks (throws only, zero plyos), the BASEBALL Block 1 'wk 8' recovery week (no plyos or throws) and deloads (Part A 1-2 sets). OBSERVED (BASEBALL season labels INFERRED).

R11 Variation changes ONE variable at a time inside a fixed pattern slot (A/B weeks, one lunge variable per week, 2-week upgrades); the slot skeleton is held inside a phase and changes at phase boundaries (BOXING wk3 new menu; AESTHETICS-12 wk8-9 drops the Mon/Thu 'TRICEP EXT.' rows and rebuilds Friday around unilateral/isolation work). OBSERVED.

R12 Intensification methods (supersets, MYO, max-rep finishers, complexes, French contrast, bands/chains) are concentrated in the last phase of hypertrophy plans and in the conversion/pre-season phases of athletic plans; never in deload weeks (exceptions: MYO preset on leg extensions in BYOP ATHLETIC week 1; contrast pairs in athletic STARTING; BASEBALL upper-body 'Superset - same reps'/'Superset - max reps' pairs, 'heavy Max reps' sets and banded lifts in all three blocks incl. Block 1 week 1 and in-season Block 3 - only the '5 of each' complexes and 'myo set' / 'myo sets' are Block-2-only). OBSERVED.

R13 Conditioning progresses by unlocking zones (C -> C+B -> C+B+A -> lactate clearance) and by density (rounds x seconds), not by making one session longer; steady cardio lives on separate days (Wed/Sat). OBSERVED.

ambiguities: He says 'this second half of the year, the second quarter': the text describes April-June, but 'second half' would be July-December. We read Q2 = April-June.

Q2 is described two ways: 'losing body fat and starting to get in shape' and 'a mix in between building up a little bit more muscle and keeping your body fat down'. Q1 is also a cut ('start the year cutting down'). Which quarter carries the main fat-loss phase: Q1, Q2 or both?

'Maintaining' in Q3: the 50-70 % maintenance volume of PER-01, or the 15-20-set 'maintenance to a little bit of growth' band of UNI-01? Our proposal (the level start) is about 66-80 % of the previous peak, so it satisfies both readings.

'Really hard work' in Q1 while cutting: should volume still step up a level in a calorie deficit? Research says a deficit blunts muscle gain but not strength gain (Murphy & Koehler 2022), so we hold the level start and put the extra work into cardio and density.

The calendar is northern-hemisphere and Christmas-based. Spanish-speaking users in the southern hemisphere (Argentina, Chile, Uruguay) have summer in December-February, and other holidays (Semana Santa, Thanksgiving, a personal vacation) may matter more.
