science_grounding.his_rule: 'The first 2 to 4 weeks are going to be just you getting used to the movements' (PER-01)
science_grounding.evidence: Damas 2016: hypertrophy signal mostly after ~3 weeks, once damage drops; repeated bout effect: early exposures protect
science_grounding.verdict: Supported. Low rate (<= 3 %) and 2-3 RIR in these weeks.

science_grounding.shape: 12-week: 4-6 weeks driving hard, last weeks hardest
science_grounding.his_rule: 'driving it hard, not all the way to the top' then 'more tired, more stimulus' (PER-01)
science_grounding.evidence: RP/Enes/Pelland: more weekly sets -> more growth with diminishing returns; Grgic 2017, Harries 2015, Moesgaard 2022: the periodization model matters little when volume is equal; Williams 2017: planned plans beat unplanned for strength
science_grounding.verdict: Supported. A volume ramp to a level cap, then load/intensity.

science_grounding.his_rule: his 12-week description has no deload; PER-05 defines the dose
science_grounding.evidence: Rogerson 2024: deload every ~5.6 weeks in practice; Bell 2023: planned or autoregulated both acceptable; Coleman 2024: a 1-week break mid-program did not change growth
science_grounding.verdict: Plausible with triggered deloads; many clients will trigger one around weeks 5-9 (open question).

science_grounding.his_rule: 'An 8-week program is a program that wants to modify you, so you have to start hard' (PER-01)
science_grounding.evidence: Scarpelli 2022 / Barsuhn 2024 (in 12_vol): trained people do well starting from their previous volume; repeated bout effect
science_grounding.verdict: Supported for people coming from recent training; after a layoff prefer the 12-week cycle (INFERRED).

science_grounding.his_rule: 'a lower-volume maintenance volume ... 70 % ... 50 %. This allows them to recover and not push too hard' (PER-01)
science_grounding.evidence: Bickel 2011 (1/3 of the dose keeps size in the young), Spiering 2021, Bosquet 2013 (strength stable ~4 weeks off), Ogasawara 2013 (breaks do not cost long-term growth)

science_grounding.his_rule: 'start at a 2 and end at an 11' (PER-01)
science_grounding.evidence: Scarpelli 2022 (progressing from the person's own previous volume worked); Pelland 2026 (each extra step of growth costs more sets); Ogasawara 2013
science_grounding.verdict: Supported with a ceiling: advanced clients climb by load, not only sets (open question).

science_grounding.his_rule: 'Just keep me in line ... and then it does it by itself' (PER-01)
science_grounding.evidence: Kiely 2012 (responsive planning), Hickmott 2022 (autoregulation as good as % plans; in 12_vol)
science_grounding.verdict: Supported when weekly logs exist (adaptive output).

science_grounding.evidence: No controlled trials of annual plans for general clients (Afonso 2017: no periodization trial longer than ~9 months); Issurin/Kiely frameworks; Murphy & Koehler 2022 (cut phases protect muscle, not grow it); Yanovski 2000 / Diaz-Zavala 2017 (holiday gain)
science_grounding.verdict: Coaching choice with sensible science support; quarter themes need his round-2 confirmation.

science_grounding.evidence: Bompa step/wave loading (practitioner); taper evidence (Bosquet 2007, Pritchard 2016); no hypertrophy advantage for any model (Grgic 2017)
science_grounding.verdict: Supported as a peaking tool; smooth stays the default elsewhere.

science_grounding.shape: Returning after a layoff (6-12+ months off) and ex-pros
science_grounding.his_rule: body treated as a beginner, skills come back fast; ex-pros at Level 1 only briefly (PRG-05)
science_grounding.evidence: Psilander 2019, Blocquiaux 2020: strength and skill persist longer than size; regaining takes about half the time off
science_grounding.verdict: Supported: L1 volume with a 4-week acclimation, exercise level kept, level-up check after the first block (PROPOSED).

science_grounding.his_rule: 'a vacation 1-week or vacation 2-week kind of thing' (PER-01)
science_grounding.evidence: Hwang 2017: strength and lean mass kept after 2 weeks off; Bosquet 2013: maximal strength mostly kept up to ~4 weeks
science_grounding.verdict: Supported: ~50 % with what is available, or full rest; return at the previous start.

science_grounding.shape: Strength %-template and Olympic ramp (PER-09: 'I just want to make sure it's correct')
science_grounding.evidence: RTS RPE chart (section 5.3); NSCA power guidance (75-85 % for 3-5 reps); Suchomel 2017 (pull variants allow heavier loads); Harries 2015 (linear steps as good as undulating for strength)
science_grounding.verdict: Main lift: consistent (loads within about 1-4 points of the chart). Olympic 4 x 8 @ 75 %: high for full catch lifts; fine for DB/KB and pull variants; flagged (14.2).

science_grounding.evidence: Issurin 2010: accumulation 2-6 weeks -> transmutation 2-4 -> realization; strength residuals ~30 +/- 5 days, explosive ~5 +/- 3 days; Painter 2012
science_grounding.verdict: Supported; keep plyos/sprints in every phase because explosive residuals are short.

volume_governor.statement_verbatim_paraphrase: People do ~15-20 sets per muscle per week; more for a muscle they want to grow, fewer with injury/pain. Volume ramps gradually week by week in ~3 %, 5 % or 7 % increments depending on the size of the muscle and the logic behind it.
volume_governor.observed_realization: The coach never writes a 3 % step. He writes whole-set steps (+25-50 % per step every 2-3 weeks) whose long-run compounded average is 4-6 %/week in his 12-week products, 2.6-3.8 %/week in the late pre-season and 3.8 %/week in the boxing conversion. The % rule is the long-run average of the step schedule (OBSERVED numbers, INFERRED reading).
volume_governor.tier_rationale: INFERRED: with typical weekly volumes in the coach's templates (quads ~16-18, chest/delts ~9-12, biceps/calves ~6-12), 3 % / 5 % / 7 % translate into about +0.35-0.85 set per muscle per week (chest/back 12 x 3 % = 0.36, quads/hams 18 x 3 % = 0.54, delts/triceps 9-12 x 5 % = 0.45-0.6, calves 6 x 7 % = 0.42, biceps 12 x 7 % = 0.84; rear delts 3 x 7 % = 0.21) = roughly +1 set every 1-3 weeks. That reproduces the observed cadence ('+1 set every 2-3 weeks') and the science that large muscles cost more systemic fatigue per set while small muscles recover faster. The REVERSE mapping (big = 7 %) would add ~1.3 sets/week to quads and ~0.36 to biceps, which matches nothing in the sheets. Coach to confirm.

floors_ceilings.maintenance_floor: INFERRED ~6-8 sets/week for hypertrophy clients (practitioner MV range; Spiering 2021: strength/size kept with ~1 set/exercise/week if intensity is kept) - not a Schoenfeld 2017 finding; athletes: whatever the slot template gives (2-8 for non-priority muscles)

floors_ceilings.science_cross_check: Baz-Valle 2022: 12-20 weekly sets optimal standard; Pelland 2025: more sets -> more growth with diminishing returns, count indirect sets as 0.5 (fractional); RP practitioner landmarks (rpstrength.com muscle guides): MEV ~4-10, MAV ~6-20, MRV ~14-26 depending on the muscle (quads MRV 14-18, chest 16-24, biceps 20-26); specialisation MRV*P up to ~24-35.

volume_governor.counting: 1 hard set = 1.0 to each prime mover + 0.5 to each clear synergist (fractional method; matches Pelland 2025). Athletic sets (plyo, throws, sprints, Olympic) are counted as EXPOSURE, not as hypertrophy sets (open question).
algorithm: 1. base_m = weekly hard sets the template gives muscle m in week 1 (plus Focus slots).
2. rate_m = tier rate after modifiers; ceiling_m = 20 (26 if focus); if base_m >= ceiling_m: hold.
3. For each loading week: target_m(w) = min(ceiling_m, target_m(w-1) * (1 + rate_m)).
4. planned_m(w) = floor(target_m(w)) (never below base_m): a whole set is released only when the accumulated increment reaches 1.0.
5. Deload week: planned = round(0.6 x previous planned) (coach range -25 % to -50 %) and the template's deload dose (3 x 8).
6. After a mid-block deload (12-week plans) the target restarts at the week-4 value of wave 1 (observed: STRENGTH-12 wk8 = wk3/4 dose; AESTHETICS-12 wk8 = 4 sets = wk4-6).

7. Assign each released set to a slot by priority: (a) the muscle's Focus slot if focus; (b) the isolation slot for SMALL/MEDIUM muscles, (c) the primary bilateral compound for LARGE muscles in hypertrophy/strength, (d) never exceed the per-slot cap (4 fat loss, 5 hypertrophy, 6-7 strength main lift) or ~20 working sets / 7-10 exercises per session.

8. Small muscles may realise the same % through reps instead of sets (FAT BURN leg ext/curl slot 15 -> 20 -> 40 -> 40; Plotkin 2022 shows rep progression is as effective as load progression, but in lower-body exercises, so it does not by itself justify a small-muscle-only rule).

retired_v0.generator_pseudocode:
generate_plan(client):
  family   = map_goal(client.goal)            # HYPERTROPHY | STRENGTH | FAT_LOSS | HYBRID | GENERAL_BEGINNER | ATHLETE
  phase    = client.season_phase if family == ATHLETE else None   # OFF | PRE | IN | TRANSITION
  shape    = SKELETONS[family(+phase)][client.weeks]              # 6 / 8 / 12 week rows (role, volume_index, reps, effort, load, methods)
  template = choose_slot_template(family, client.days, client.sport, client.equipment)   # e.g. AESTHETICS 4-day, ATHLETIC 4-day, PPL 6-day
  base     = level_base(client.level)          # sets/exercise 2 (beginner) / 3 (intermediate+); athlete level dial for ATHLETE
  for week in shape:
     for slot in template.slots:
        ex      = pick_exercise(slot, tier=slot_tier[slot], variation=variation_rule(family, phase, week), history)
        sets    = base * week.volume_index/100  (STEP mode)  -> rounded, capped per slot (4 FL / 5 HYP / 6-7 STR main)
        reps    = week.reps[ex.class]            # compound wave vs isolation rule (inverse legend)
        effort  = EFFORT_BY_CLASS[ex.class] adjusted by week.effort
        load    = week.load if family == STRENGTH or ex.is_olympic else implicit
     apply_governor(SMOOTH mode for focus muscles; ceilings 20 / 26; pain/deficit/in-season modifiers)
     add_athletic_block(week.plyo_zone, contacts target, throws, sprint density)   # ATHLETE / HYBRID
     add_conditioning(aerobic level unlock, density progression, separate days)
     if week.role == DELOAD: apply D4 (3 x 8, RPE 7, drop methods/conditioning/Oly, Part A 1-2 sets)
  after each logged week: autoregulate(EFFORT, HOW IT FELT?) -> adjust next week; early deload if D11 fires

athletic_quality_rules_v1.rule: Own budget: plyos, ballistics, throws, Olympic lifts and sprints never count toward muscle sets; counted as contacts, reps, throws, meters

Ballistic -> plyometric: programs start more ballistic and become more plyometric (connective tissue). Plyo:ballistic share by the sport's ground-contact time: more ground time (karate, fighters) -> more ballistics; less (sprinters) -> more plyos; basketball a mix; baseball ballistics + rotational + sprinting, few plyos
athletic_quality_rules_v1.tag: COACH-ANSWER CAT-10, ATH-01, ATH-02; shares PROPOSED (12_volume_algorithm_v1 §3.13)

athletic_quality_rules_v1.rule: Plyo method stages (not zones): stage 1 receive & pause, stage 2 receive then create once, stage 3 repeatedly receive and create; bilateral before unilateral (unilateral is harder). Name pending; PROPOSED 'Receive-Create stages' RC1-RC3, weeks 1-2 / 3-5 / 6+ of a cycle (12-week off-season: RC3 bilateral weeks 6-8, unilateral weeks 9-12). Davidson zones do not apply to plyos

Olympic lifts for everyone in athletic training: L1 DB/KB snatches, hex-bar jumps, hang pulls/cleans; L2+ hang power -> full 'Squat Snatch' / 'Squat Clean' / 'Squat Clean & Jerk'; push press easier, push jerk intermediate/advanced; youth may lift from the floor; % ramp 75 -> 90 % per 4-week block for L2+. In-season: open question
athletic_quality_rules_v1.tag: COACH-ANSWER ATH-10, LIB-07, LIB-13, ATH-09, PER-09

athletic_quality_rules_v1.rule: Throws: no levels; light balls (8-10 lb) for speed, never over 20 lb; none for aesthetics/bodybuilders except warm-up; high volume for baseball, boxing, MMA, tennis, golf
Contrast / French contrast / complexes: intermediate+ athletes, off-season only, heavy lift ~78-85 %, no rest inside the complex (fight-camp use: round-2 question)
In-season athletic work: sprints for speed athletes, (high) jumps for jumping athletes, strength maintenance for others
Older clients: few plyos unless they ask; no sex-based rules (age, foundation, goal, injuries decide)
Change of direction: route tiers EASY -> MOD. -> HARD TURN apply to every athlete

Aerobic: 3 sessions/week general/fat loss, 2 athletes in-season, 4 aesthetics/bodybuilders plus long walks after workouts; off-season VO2/mitochondrial work can come from supersets; fighters' session-opening cardio is a real aerobic block; any erg, by calories, time or distance
No bands: reverse-banded (assisted/overspeed) plyos and banded throws/chops are out of scope

exercise_progression_rules_v1.rule: Blocks of 4-6 weeks: exercises fixed inside a block; the next block changes one or two of grip, stance, implement, range of motion or rep range, never all at once
A/B lead-lift weeks (squat-led / hinge-led; bench / overhead) are an option for people who want variety, in any program; off by default

Second exposure of a slot in a week = a different exercise from the same category; axial spinal loading once a week (squat one day, leg press or belt squat the other; deadlifts count as spinal loading)

Level up a slot at the end of a block if it felt '8 - That was perfect' or easier with no pain; levels are still theoretical; client level and exercise level are separate; a higher level keeps the lower options

Exercise level reads from skill, stability and load position: front-loaded/low = foundational, load on the body/horizontal = intermediate, behind the body/overhead = advanced; machines and cables are easier

Choice between alternatives: by client profile (older/injured -> machines or DBs; experienced -> barbell) and by the client's preference. Machines are NOT ranked (brands and angles differ): hack squat and leg press are more constrained than the Smith machine; belt squat avoids axial loading (use it when the back is already loaded or sore); GHD / reverse hyper if available and the client feels the right muscles

Older / injured / high-volume clients collect volume on constrained machines (constraint 4-5) and never get overhead squat, snatch, low-bar squat or depth jumps; they may use machines filed at any level

Bilateral:unilateral share across blocks: bodybuilders/powerlifters ~50/50 in block 1 with contra/ipsi health work in the first 2-4 weeks -> 80/20-90/10; field/COD athletes 80-90 % unilateral; in-season minimal bilateral; adjustable 90/10 to 10/90; pain shifts it

exercise_progression_rules_v1.rule: Contralateral load pulls into the hip (change-of-direction athletes: football, soccer, basketball, tennis); ipsilateral helps out of the hip (sprint acceleration: ipsilateral step-ups)
Pain: swap within the category to a more constrained, split-grip or unilateral variant and keep the sets if possible; then cut 30-50 %; then drop the exercise
No bands or variable resistance (bands, chains, weight releasers) in any variation or substitution
